title: Reservation lifecycle orchestration with adaptive throughput guarantees
creator: Nora Thompson
description: Build an orchestration flow for dedicated capacity reservation requests that attaches adaptive throughput guarantees and integrates approvals, autoscaling policy templates, and fleet controls. This ticket defines the end-to-end lifecycle (request -> validation -> approval/auto-approval -> provisioning -> SLA binding -> post-provision adjustments) and delivers a prescriptive playbook and API contract for intake, automated decisions, and manual escalation paths. The goal is to reduce approval latency for low-risk requests, codify throughput guarantees per reservation tier, and enable operational controls for fleet balancing and preemptive capacity adjustments.
acceptance_criteria: Intake API accepts reservation requests with workload profile metadata (qps, p50/p95 latency goals, typical sequence length, KV cache reuse estimate)
Auto-approval rules implemented for low-risk requests (<= X GPUs, standard image, no sensitive data flags) with audit trail
Reservation objects are created with a throughput_guarantee field and bindable SLA template
Autoscaling policy templates (conservative, balanced, aggressive) available and selectable at request time
Fleet controls include reserve/capacity-escrow, preempt policy, and migration window metadata
Operational dashboard shows pending approvals, active guarantees, utilization vs. committed throughput, and early-warning signals
End-to-end tests that simulate burst traffic validate autoscaling decisions and fallback to lower-cost variants without violating guaranteed availability
implementation_notes: Define a compact reservation schema (reservation_id, owner, workload_profile, throughput_guarantee, policy_template, start/stop windows, billing_anchor)
Auto-approval engine uses deterministic checks: resource footprint threshold, historical spend sanity, verified billing info, no compliance flags
Introduce a reservation states machine: requested -> validated -> approved/auto-approved -> provisioning -> active -> adjusting -> decommissioning
Provisioning pipeline must tag infra with SLA metadata for runtime routing (priority queues + KV cache retention)
Expose audit logs to customer (read-only) and internal billing/ops teams (full trace)
Create three default autoscale templates based on throughput targets and latency SLOs and make them extensible by ENG owners
decisions: Use an adaptive throughput_guarantee (tokens/sec) rather than fixed vGPU counts to give operators flexibility in bin-packing
Auto-approval will be allowed up to 4x typical free-tier GPU units for signed customers where billing and TOS checks pass
SLA binding attaches both an availability percentage and an ops response SLA for incident escalation
Default preempt policy is 'graceful-evict' with a 15-minute migration window unless tenant opts into 'immediate-evict' for cost savings
risks: Overly permissive auto-approval could exhaust shared capacity spikes; mitigated by dynamic caps tied to current fleet headroom
Complexity in mapping throughput guarantees to heterogeneous hardware might cause mismatch between promised and delivered throughput
Billing reconciliation gaps if reserved throughput is scaled mid-billing-cycle without clear anchor rules
Customer confusion if capacity upgrades/downgrades change routing and KV cache hit behavior leading to subtle regressions in latency
